builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: NextEval: An Agent-Based Solver and Benchmark for Derivative-Free Optimization
summary: Replaces hand-tuned selection and configuration of derivative-free optimization methods (e.g., Bayesian optimization or direct-search solvers) with an LLM agent that chooses tools, sets parameters, and allocates evaluation budget from a shared history. Costs LLM API calls per optimization step plus the engineering of a numerical environment with tools and persistent state, adding per-iteration latency and orchestration complexity on top of the objective evaluations themselves. Can fail through poor LLM tool selection or parameter choices, API cost and rate limits under large evaluation budgets, and gains demonstrated only on low-dimensional problems that may not transfer to higher-dimensional or noisier objectives.
rationale: The approach is reproducible with third-party LLM APIs and no GPU training, but its advantage over mature open-source DFO baselines must be validated on the reader's specific objective functions and evaluation budgets before production adoption.

claims.statement: Replaces hand-tuned selection and configuration of derivative-free optimization methods (e.g., Bayesian optimization or direct-search solvers) with an LLM agent that chooses tools, sets parameters, and allocates evaluation budget from a shared history. Costs LLM API calls per optimization step plus the engineering of a numerical environment with tools and persistent state, adding per-iteration latency and orchestration complexity on top of the objective evaluations themselves. Can fail through poor LLM tool selection or parameter choices, API cost and rate limits under large evaluation budgets, and gains demonstrated only on low-dimensional problems that may not transfer to higher-dimensional or noisier objectives.

The abstract states that on low-dimensional DFO problems the NextEval solver outperforms state-of-the-art DFO baselines in function-evaluation efficiency, with no numeric factor reported in the abstract.
